story.title: Lost in the Amusement Park
paragraphs_en: Boing! Boing! Boing! “Justin! Stop bouncing on the bed!” demanded Justin’s mum Annie, stomping her foot and putting her hands on her hips angrily. “But this is so fun!” giggled Justin playfully. Justin was very excited for his seven years old birthday celebration at the amusement park tomorrow. Merely thinking of it got him very, very hyped. This was going to be one long night for Justin.

“Time to go!” called Annie as she headed to the door. “Wait for me!” yelled Justin, holding up one arm and dashing towards the door like Superman. “Wheeeeeeee” cried Justin, screaming his head off. He went blue on his face, his mouth was all dry, it was like a giant hair dryer! And his eyes were stinging when he tried to open them. When Annie and Justin got off the roller coaster, Justin’s knees were still shaking!!!

“Mom, can I have a chocolate ice cream with sprinkles?” asked Justin. “What? It’s $100!” exclaimed Annie, still feeling a bit dizzy from the rollercoaster ride. “Silly mom, that’s just $10.” Justin said. “Ok, here you go,” replied Annie giving him $10. After the ice cream break, they had a lot of fun going on rides and playing games. Justin’s favorite ride was the Ferris wheel, and his favorite game was the ring toss.

“Mom, what’s next?” asked Justin. “Let’s go to the spinning cups,” answered Annie. Then they passed by a clown performance. “Mum, can we watch a bit?” asked Justin. Annie nodded. “Yipee!” exclaimed Justin, as they headed toward the show. “Ha! Ha! Ha! Ha!” Justin laughed loudly as he watched the clowns got into some silly fights when the show was over the whole audience couldn’t stop laughing!

Annie grabbed on Justin’s hand, and said, “Okay, let’s go Justin.” They were walking through a crowd and Annie was going too fast. Justin got squeezed and shoved that he couldn’t move forward along with his mom. “Mommy, you’re going too fast!” Justin cried. But it was too late. His hand slipped of mom’s and her hand fell onto another boy’s hand. When the crowd cleared up. The little boy was shrieked, “Where are you taking me?” “Oh! I am sorry!” answered Annie in puzzle and brought the frightened boy back to his mother. That’s when Annie realised that she had lost Justin!

As for Justin, he was feeling very miserable indeed. He started sniffling and calling, “Mommy where are you?” Tears began to well in his eyes, his lips started to wobble, and his forehead and hands started to sweat. “Waaaaaaaa!” he sobbed. Then suddenly, he saw the spinning cup ride. “Oh right! Mummy said something about the spinning cup!” he thought and he dashed right to the ride.

At the spinning cup ride, Justin couldn’t find his mum. Tears started rolling down his face. A kind ride operator kneeled down and asked, “Hello little boy, how can I help you? What happened?” After Justin told her exactly what happened, she stood up and said, “Follow me.” “But where are we going?” asked Justin.

“This is my boss,” introduced the kind ride operator whose name was Nancy. “Hello boss,” greeted Justin. “Don’t call me boss, call me Mark,” chuckled the boss. “But where is mummy?” mumbled Justin who was getting quieter and quieter. Then all of a sudden he started sniffling, and putting his hands on his face. “We are going to bring you to the loudspeaker, so you can call your mum," comforted Mark. “Mmmm, okay,” nodded Justin.

Annie couldn’t find Justin. Then suddenly she recalled what she said to Justin before the clown performance. Feeling very lucky, she sprinted to a teahouse called Spinning Cup. At the teahouse, Annie spun around and almost knocked over a waitress. “Madam, how can I help you?” said the kind waitress. But before Annie could reply, the announcement began.

“Good afternoon, All guests of Spinning Amusement Park. Today, a boy named Justin got lost. If you are his mother, please go to the fifth floor of the general office.” Then Mark gave the megaphone to Justin. But all Justin could say was a loud shrieking “WHAAAAA” “Oh! That’s Justin!” Annie shouted. And before she knew it, everyone in the restaurant was staring at her. Annie was very, very, truly embarrassed (even though she was really excited to hear Justin's voice). In seconds, she sprinted to the general office.

“Mama mama , I miss you!” sniffled Justin happily. Holding up his arms and running toward Annie, crying with joy, like he found his favorite teddy bear! After thanking Mark, Annie and Justin left. “Let’s go to the Spinning Cups now,” suggested Annie. “Ok!” laughed Justin and hugged his mom. He was happy to have a fun mum. On the way to the Spinning Cups, Justin said to Annie, “You know mummy, next time I’ll keep calm when I am lost. And think more clearly.” “I am glad to hear that!” answered Annie.

“What? It’s $100!” exclaimed Annie, still feeling a bit dizzy from the rollercoaster ride.
“Silly mom, that’s just $10.” Justin said.
“Ok, here you go,” replied Annie giving him $10.
After the ice cream break, they had a lot of fun going on rides and playing games.
Justin’s favorite ride was the Ferris wheel, and his favorite game was the ring toss.
“Mom, what’s next?” asked Justin.
“Let’s go to the spinning cups,” answered Annie.
Then they passed by a clown performance.
“Mum, can we watch a bit?” asked Justin.
Annie nodded. “Yipee!” exclaimed Justin, as they headed toward the show.
“Ha! Ha! Ha!
Ha!” Justin laughed loudly as he watched the clowns got into some silly fights when the show was over the whole audience couldn’t stop laughing!
Annie grabbed on Justin’s hand, and said, “Okay, let’s go Justin.” They were walking through a crowd and Annie was going too fast.
Justin got squeezed and shoved that he couldn’t move forward along with his mom.
“Mommy, you’re going too fast!” Justin cried.
But it was too late.
His hand slipped of mom’s and her hand fell onto another boy’s hand.
When the crowd cleared up.
The little boy was shrieked, “Where are you taking me?” “Oh!
I am sorry!” answered Annie in puzzle and brought the frightened boy back to his mother.
That’s when Annie realised that she had lost Justin!
As for Justin, he was feeling very miserable indeed.
He started sniffling and calling, “Mommy where are you?” Tears began to well in his eyes, his lips started to wobble, and his forehead and hands started to sweat.
“Waaaaaaaa!” he sobbed.
Then suddenly, he saw the spinning cup ride.
“Oh right! Mummy said something about the spinning cup!” he thought and he dashed right to the ride.
At the spinning cup ride, Justin couldn’t find his mum.
Tears started rolling down his face.
A kind ride operator kneeled down and asked, “Hello little boy, how can I help you?
What happened?” After Justin told her exactly what happened, she stood up and said, “Follow me.” “But where are we going?” asked Justin.
“This is my boss,” introduced the kind ride operator whose name was Nancy.
“Hello boss,” greeted Justin.
“Don’t call me boss, call me Mark,” chuckled the boss.
“But where is mummy?” mumbled Justin who was getting quieter and quieter.
Then all of a sudden he started sniffling, and putting his hands on his face.
“We are going to bring you to the loudspeaker, so you can call your mum," comforted Mark.
“Mmmm, okay,” nodded Justin.
Annie couldn’t find Justin.
Then suddenly she recalled what she said to Justin before the clown performance.
Feeling very lucky, she sprinted to a teahouse called Spinning Cup.
At the teahouse, Annie spun around and almost knocked over a waitress.
“Madam, how can I help you?” said the kind waitress.
But before Annie could reply, the announcement began.
“Good afternoon, All guests of Spinning Amusement Park.
Today, a boy named Justin got lost.
If you are his mother, please go to the fifth floor of the general office.” Then Mark gave the megaphone to Justin.
But all Justin could say was a loud shrieking “WHAAAAA” “Oh!
That’s Justin!” Annie shouted.
And before she knew it, everyone in the restaurant was staring at her.
Annie was very, very, truly embarrassed (even though she was really excited to hear Justin's voice).
In seconds, she sprinted to the general office.
“Mama mama , I miss you!” sniffled Justin happily.
Holding up his arms and running toward Annie, crying with joy, like he found his favorite teddy bear!
After thanking Mark, Annie and Justin left.
“Let’s go to the Spinning Cups now,” suggested Annie.
“Ok!” laughed Justin and hugged his mom.
He was happy to have a fun mum.
On the way to the Spinning Cups, Justin said to Annie, “You know mummy, next time I’ll keep calm when I am lost.
And think more clearly.” “I am glad to hear that!” answered Annie.
